plan:
- Single Board Computer (e.g., Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W or similar) for core processing, Wi-Fi, and Bluetooth.
- Touchscreen display (small, e.g., 3.5-5 inch) for interface.
- Lithium Polymer battery and associated charging/power management module (e.g., LiPo HAT) for portability.
- USB WiFi adapter (if SBC doesn't have sufficient built-in capability) for signal capture/analysis.
- Custom 3D-printed compact enclosure to house all components, with cutouts for ports and screen.
- Small tactile buttons or joystick for additional user input, integrated into the enclosure.

originalPrompt: A Hacking Tool with a Screen, battery life, it Must can Control speakers via Bluetooth and can go into W-lan. It Must can catch Signals of other devices and it Must be cheap

subSteps.title: 3D print all mechanical components according to specified settings
Clean and deburr all 3D printed parts, removing supports and imperfections
Install M3 brass heat-set inserts into designated holes in the enclosure bottom shell
Test-fit the SBC mount with the main_sbc and the display frame with the touch_display
Test-fit the joystick and button bezels with their respective input modules and buttons
Prepare and solder wires to the joystick module pins (VCC, GND, VRX, VRY, SW)
Prepare and solder wires to each tactile button (Signal, GND)
Connect the Li-Po battery to the power management HAT via the JST-PH connector
Connect the power management HAT GPIO (I2C/Power) to the main_sbc GPIO (I2C) pins
Connect the joystick input and all button wires to the appropriate GPIO pins on the main_sbc
Connect the main_sbc to the touch_display via HDMI for video and USB for touch data
Connect the main_sbc to external power (USB-C) and verify boot-up and OS functionality
Connect the external Wi-Fi adapter to the main_sbc and verify its recognition and connectivity
Power the touch_display externally (Micro USB) and verify video output from main_sbc via HDMI
Verify touch input functionality on the display via the USB connection to the main_sbc
Verify I2C communication and basic power management functions between main_sbc and power_management HAT
Test all joystick and tactile button inputs, ensuring correct GPIO assignment and responsiveness
Verify the system can power on and off using the power management HAT and Li-Po battery
Mount the main_sbc onto the SBC mount using appropriate screws
Mount the touch_display into the display frame, securing it with M2.5 screws if applicable
Mount the Li-Po battery into the battery tray and secure the power management HAT onto its mount
Mount the external Wi-Fi adapter onto its mount
Secure the SBC mount, Li-Po battery tray, power management mount, and Wi-Fi adapter mount into the enclosure bottom shell using M2.5 screws
Route all internal cables (HDMI, USB, GPIO, power) neatly and apply strain relief where necessary
Snap-fit the joystick and button bezels with their respective components into the enclosure top bezel
Attach the display frame with the touch_display to the enclosure top bezel (clips/M2.5 screws) and then close the enclosure top bezel onto the bottom shell using M3 flat head screws

projectDescription: A compact, battery-powered hacking tool integrates an SBC, 5-inch capacitive touchscreen, and high-gain WiFi for W-LAN access and signal capture. Housed in a 3D-printed enclosure, it features joystick and button controls for Bluetooth speaker manipulation.

imagePromptSnapshot.description:
Project idea: A Hacking Tool with a Screen, battery life, it Must can Control speakers via Bluetooth and can go into W-lan. It Must can catch Signals of other devices and it Must be cheap

Design notes: Hacking tool, Screen, Battery life, Bluetooth speaker control, Wi-Fi access, Signal capture, Compact form factor, Cheap

Electrical components (current): Main Controller SBC (mcu, 85x56x17mm); 5-inch Capacitive Touch Display (display, 121x76x10mm); 2x power: Li-Po Power Management HAT, Rechargeable Li-Po Battery; High-Gain USB WiFi Adapter (module, 85x25x10mm); 6x sensor: Mini Joystick Module, Tactile Button (Up), Tactile Button (Down), Tactile Button (Left) +2 more

Mechanical/structural parts (current): 13x 3d_printed: Enclosure Bottom Shell, Enclosure Top Bezel, SBC Mount, Display Frame +9 more; 3x misc: M3 Brass Heat-Set Insert, M3 Flat Head Screw 10mm, M2.5 Flat Head Screw 6mm

Assembly: Enclosure Bottom Shell → M3 Brass Heat-Set Insert (press-fitted); Enclosure Bottom Shell → SBC Mount (M2.5 screws); Enclosure Bottom Shell → Li-Po Battery Tray (M2.5 screws); Enclosure Bottom Shell → Power Management Mount (M2.5 screws); Enclosure Bottom Shell → WiFi Adapter Mount (M2.5 screws); Enclosure Top Bezel → Enclosure Bottom Shell (M3 flat head screws into heat-set inserts); Enclosure Top Bezel → Display Frame (clips/M2.5 screws); Enclosure Top Bezel → Joystick Bezel (clips/snap-fit); Enclosure Top Bezel → Button Up Bezel (clips/snap-fit); Enclosure Top Bezel → Button Down Bezel (clips/snap-fit); Enclosure Top Bezel → Button Left Bezel (clips/snap-fit); Enclosure Top Bezel → Button Right Bezel (clips/snap-fit); Enclosure Top Bezel → Button Enter Bezel (clips/snap-fit); M3 Flat Head Screw 10mm → Enclosure Top Bezel (passes through); M3 Flat Head Screw 10mm → M3 Brass Heat-Set Insert (threaded connection) (+16 more connections)

tools: Heat gun or soldering iron with flat tip (for heat-set inserts)
Small hobby knife or deburring tool
HDMI cable (suitable for SBC to display)
USB-A to USB-Micro B cable (for display touch)
USB-A extension cable or adapter (for WiFi adapter)
assumptions: Basic 3D printing knowledge and printer calibration
Basic soldering experience for small components and wires
Familiarity with Linux command line for SBC configuration
Micro SD card with a compatible operating system for the Main Controller SBC is prepared
Appropriate GPIO breakout cables or jumper wires are available for connecting peripherals to the main_sbc
